description: Create a draft link-building outreach campaign (sends via the user's connected Gmail). Outreach flow: 1) interview the user (their site, goal, competitors), 2) build a prospect list with get_competitor_gap / get_referring_domains / get_domain_authority, 3) research one real contact email per prospect domain, 4) write a short personalized subject+body per contact, 5) outreach_create_campaign, 6) outreach_add_contacts, 7) show the user the emails you drafted and get their OK before launching, 8) outreach_launch_campaign: this tells RankParse the campaign is ready and returns status ready_for_review with a review_url (the campaign page), and nothing is sent until the user approves the emails there one by one; tell the user it is ready to review in RankParse and share the review_url (if status is approved it is already approved, so do not launch again). Shortcut: propose_outreach_send does steps 5, 6 and 8 in one call (creates or tops up the campaign, adds the contacts, marks it ready for review). Requires the user to have Gmail connected at rankparse.com/dashboard/integrations. To CONTINUE an existing campaign rather than start a new one, begin at outreach_suggest_prospects instead of step 1: campaigns are topped up, not replaced. To change the email copy of contacts already in a campaign (for example when the user asks for a rewrite), call outreach_update_contacts on the SAME campaign and then outreach_launch_campaign again; never create a second campaign for that, because the first one would keep its old unsent emails.

goal.description: What the outreach is trying to achieve, for the campaign record

name.description: Campaign name, e.g. "SaaS blogs - competitor gap Aug 2026"

site_id.description: Optional RankParse website id (from list_websites, or given to you in a website-scoped outreach prompt) to link this campaign to a website. Omit to leave it unassigned.

name: outreach_create_campaign
